final_candidates.decision_summary: Strongest LOF signal (0.959); Gly->Arg at a conserved translocation-relevant position likely abolishes substrate transport. PLM scores it as a disruptive but plausible single change compatible with membrane-protein biogenesis.

High LOF proxy (0.888) with the best evolutionary tolerance among damaging candidates, indicating disruption without gross instability. Charge reversal in the extracellular loop is a classic transporter-silencing substitution.
Pathogenic-class LOF prediction (0.721) via a conservative charge-neutralizing swap that minimizes folding risk. Conservative nature slightly reduces confidence in complete transport ablation.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 ordering is stable across phenotype, MSA, and PLM evidence; further calls are unlikely to change the outcome.

history.rationale: Analog of the naturally occurring reduced-function allele R61C; Arg-to-Cys in the large extracellular loop disrupts substrate interaction while natural occurrence implies preserved abundance.

Homologs tolerate C at this position (~4.6% frequency, good coverage), so protein viability is plausible; the near-zero ESM-1v plausibility is consistent with strong functional disruption, which is the desired LOF direction. This mirrors a known naturally occurring reduced-function OCT1 variant class.
AlphaMissense classifies R60C as benign (0.268), directly contradicting the transport-ablation objective despite favorable conservation scores.

rejection.reason: AlphaMissense classifies R60C as benign (0.268), directly contradicting the transport-ablation objective despite favorable conservation scores.

history.rationale: Analog of the known loss-of-function allele C88R; replacing a conserved cysteine likely perturbs loop structure/translocation without triggering full misfolding.

Highest MSA mutant frequency (12.9%) among candidates with excellent coverage indicates evolutionary tolerance of the residue at this site; ESM-1v strongly disfavors it, consistent with loss of transport function rather than gross misfolding.

LOF proxy 0.888 plus the best evolutionary and PLM tolerance among damaging candidates, suggesting disruption without gross instability. Charge reversal in the extracellular loop is a classic transporter-silencing move.
Analog of the reduced-function allele G465R in transmembrane helix 11; introducing a charged Arg into the pore-lining face blocks transport yet is tolerated as a natural variant.

The glycine-to-arginine change in a transmembrane substrate-pocket region is strongly disfavored by both ESM-1v and MSA, predicting functional disruption; low alignment coverage (0.36) weakens the viability evidence, so confidence is slightly reduced pending direct LOF/viability signals.

AlphaMissense LOF proxy 0.959 is the strongest transport-ablation signal in the pool. Gly->Arg at a conserved loop position likely disrupts substrate translocation while remaining a single-residue change compatible with membrane insertion.
Analog of the G401S reduced-function allele in TMH10; conservative Gly-to-Ser can impair conformational cycling needed for transport.
Serine occurs at ~7.8% frequency among covered homologs, supporting folding/abundance, while ESM-1v disfavors the substitution consistent with impaired transport.
Ambiguous LOF proxy (0.525) and weak conservation support; retained only as backup.
Analog of the R488M reduced-function allele; mutation of a basic pore-lining residue reduces substrate recognition while preserving membrane insertion.
ESM-1v rates it as fully plausible (1.0), i.e., likely near-neutral with little functional disruption, which fails the primary LOF objective.

rejection.reason: ESM-1v rates it as fully plausible (1.0), i.e., likely near-neutral with little functional disruption, which fails the primary LOF objective.

history.rationale: Charge-neutralizing substitution at a conserved acidic position near the intracellular substrate vestibule, expected to reduce cation translocation with conservative chemistry.
Conservative charge-neutral change may not abolish transport; MSA shows zero Q tolerance with weak coverage, giving ambiguous signal.

Pathogenic-class LOF prediction (0.721) with a conservative charge-neutralizing substitution that minimizes folding risk. Conservative swap reduces misfolding probability but may yield incomplete ablation.
Basic residue in the intracellular loop/TMH10 region that may participate in substrate gating; conservative neutralization may reduce transport while keeping structure intact.
Charge-neutralizing mutation is sequence-model-disfavored but with poor MSA coverage; uncertain whether effect is functional or structural, so downgraded.
Ambiguous phenotype score and poor evolutionary tolerance make it a weak LOF candidate.
Aromatic residue in the substrate pocket; Trp-to-Phe retains hydrophobic packing and folding but removes H-bonding capacity that may be needed for translocation.
Conservative aromatic substitution with moderate homolog tolerance, but weak evidence of transport ablation; kept as a backup pending phenotype evidence.
Benign LOF prediction (0.264); aromatic-conservative substitution unlikely to abolish transport.

rejection.reason: Benign LOF prediction (0.264); aromatic-conservative substitution unlikely to abolish transport.
